draft_passage: the barbarian sound of enormous drums came from her forecastle; the mates and harpooneers danced with the olive-hued girls eloped from the Polynesian Isles
source_has: a crowd of her men were seen standing round her huge try-pots, which, covered with the parchment-like poke or stomach skin of the black fish, gave forth a loud roar to every stroke of the clenched hands of the crew
why_damaged: The draft mentions drums but removes the explanation that the crew were beating on try-pot skins to produce them, so the source of the 'barbarian sound' is inexplicable.

draft_passage: Next day four whales were slain—one by Ahab.
source_has: Not seldom in this life, when, on the right side, fortune's favourites sail close by us…So seemed it with the Pequod. For next day after encountering the gay Bachelor, whales were seen and four were slain
why_damaged: The source's opening philosophical paragraph establishes that the Bachelor's luck rubbed off on the Pequod, causally linking the encounter to the whale sightings; the draft drops this framing entirely, leaving the sudden whale-abundance unexplained.

draft_passage: For that strange spectacle—the head turned sunwards—conveyed a new wondrousness.
source_has: For that strange spectacle observable in all sperm whales dying—the turning sunwards of the head, and so expiring—that strange spectacle, beheld of such a placid evening, somehow to Ahab conveyed a wondrousness unknown before.
why_damaged: The draft drops 'observable in all sperm whales dying,' removing the generalizing cetological context that explains why the narrator pauses to remark on this spectacle at all.

draft_passage: where for long Chinese ages the billows have still rolled on speechless and unspoken to, as stars that shine upon the Niger's unknown source; but see! no sooner dead than death whirls round the corpse, and it heads another way.
source_has: here, too, life dies sunwards full of faith; but see! no sooner dead, than death whirls round the corpse, and it heads some other way.
why_damaged: The draft removes 'here, too, life dies sunwards full of faith,' which is the positive term of the contrast that the 'but see!' then overturns; without it the adversative 'but' has no antecedent clause to oppose.

draft_passage: In vain, oh whale, dost thou seek intercedings with yon all-quickening sun.
source_has: In vain, oh whale, dost thou seek intercedings with yon all-quickening sun, that only calls forth life, but gives it not again.
why_damaged: The draft cuts the subordinate clause explaining why the sun cannot help the whale, leaving the assertion 'in vain' without the logical reason given in the source.

draft_passage: but see! no sooner dead than death whirls round the corpse, and it heads another way.
source_has: here, too, life dies sunwards full of faith; but see! no sooner dead, than death whirls round the corpse, and it heads some other way.
why_damaged: The draft cuts 'here, too, life dies sunwards full of faith,' which is the pivot-clause completing the rhetorical accumulation and providing the contrast that 'but see!' reacts against; without it the logical opposition collapses.

draft_passage: In vain, oh whale, dost thou seek intercedings with yon all-quickening sun.
source_has: In vain, oh whale, dost thou seek intercedings with yon all-quickening sun, that only calls forth life, but gives it not again.
why_damaged: The explanatory relative clause 'that only calls forth life, but gives it not again' is cut, removing the stated reason why the whale's intercession is in vain and leaving the declaration unsupported.

draft_passage: The waif-pole was thrust upright into the dead whale's spout-hole; and the lantern hanging from its top, cast a troubled flickering glare upon the black, glossy back…
source_has: The four whales slain that evening had died wide apart… the windward one could not be reached till morning; and the boat that had killed it lay by its side all night; and that boat was Ahab's.
why_damaged: The entire opening paragraph establishing which whale is being watched, why it is isolated from the ship, and why Ahab's boat is spending the night alongside it has been dropped, so the waif-pole scene and Ahab's nocturnal vigil have no spatial or situational grounding.

draft_passage: Handling his cabalistical toy, he muttered: "Foolish toy! babies' plaything of haughty Admirals…"
source_has: Then gazing at his quadrant, and handling, one after the other, its numerous cabalistical contrivances, he pondered again
why_damaged: The draft never names the object as the quadrant before Ahab's speech begins, so a reader cannot identify what instrument he is handling when he starts muttering.

draft_passage: A sneering triumph seemed meant for Ahab, a fatalistic despair for himself, on the Parsee's mute face as he glided away.
source_has: these passed over the mute, motionless Parsee's face. Unobserved he rose and glided away
why_damaged: The draft collapses the sequence so the expressions appear to occur during the gliding away rather than before it, and drops 'Unobserved he rose,' which explains how the Parsee departed without anyone noticing.

draft_passage: A voice answered through an interval of blackness and thunder: "Old Thunder!"—Ahab, groping to his pivot-hole
why_damaged: Starbuck's prior question 'Who's there?' is cut, so 'a voice answered' has nothing it is answering, and 'Old Thunder' reads as a mysterious exclamation rather than a self-identifying reply.

draft_passage: flinching from a swash that jammed his hand; but catching sight of the flames, he changed: "The corpusants have mercy on us all!"
source_has: immediately shifting his tone he cried—"The corpusants have mercy on us all!"
why_damaged: The phrase 'he changed' is vague and ambiguous where the source says 'immediately shifting his tone,' leaving the reader unsure whether Stubb changed position, direction, or manner.

draft_passage: Starbuck, going forward, pushed against Stubb. "What thinkest thou now, man?"
source_has: "What thinkest thou now, man; I heard thy cry; it was not the same in the song."
why_damaged: The draft cuts Starbuck's contrasting observation ('I heard thy cry; it was not the same in the song'), so his question loses its meaning and the reader cannot understand what contrast Starbuck is drawing.

draft_passage: Again the high tapering flames leaped with redoubled pallor.
source_has: At that moment Starbuck caught sight of Stubb's face slowly beginning to glimmer into sight. Glancing upwards, he cried: "See! see!" and once more the high tapering flames were beheld
why_damaged: The draft drops Starbuck's 'See! see!' exclamation and its trigger (Stubb's face glimmering into sight), so the renewed appearance of the flames has no narrative cause or observer to anchor it.

draft_passage: Overhearing him, the panic-stricken crew ran to the braces—though no sail was left.
source_has: Overhearing Starbuck, the panic-stricken crew instantly ran to the braces
why_damaged: The draft substitutes 'him' for 'Starbuck,' but the immediately preceding speaker in the draft is Ahab, making the antecedent of 'him' ambiguous or misleading.
